stem: A 46-year-old man develops fatigue and fasting hypoglycemia several months after pituitary surgery. Secondary adrenal insufficiency is suspected. Which hormone pattern is most consistent with this diagnosis?

options.label: A
options.misconception: None; pituitary ACTH deficiency reduces adrenal cortisol production.
options.explanation: Damage to the pituitary can lower ACTH, so the adrenal cortex receives less stimulation to produce cortisol.

options.label: B
options.misconception: This is the loss-of-feedback pattern of primary adrenal failure.
options.explanation: When the adrenal gland itself fails, low cortisol removes feedback and ACTH rises.

options.label: C
options.misconception: This pattern implies cortisol excess suppressing ACTH, not adrenal insufficiency.
options.explanation: High cortisol would be inconsistent with the suspected cortisol-deficient state.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Both hormones being high suggests persistent stimulation or loss of normal regulation.
options.explanation: Secondary adrenal insufficiency is defined by inadequate pituitary stimulation, so ACTH should not be high.

options.label: E
options.misconception: A normal ACTH value can be inappropriate in context, but high cortisol rules out this deficiency pattern.
options.explanation: The expected central-deficiency pattern is low ACTH accompanied by low cortisol.

context: Learning objective: distinguish central from primary adrenal insufficiency using the direction of ACTH and cortisol changes. Pituitary failure causes inadequate ACTH secretion, which reduces adrenal cortisol synthesis; primary adrenal failure instead produces a compensatory ACTH rise.
